items.title: NIK C2: The new AI-enabled command-and-control framework
items.body:

Cisco Talos observed a new AI-integrated command-and-control (C2) framework in the wild called “NIK C2.” NIK C2 contains a Windows implant, using which, an actor can dump credentials, stream the victim's keystrokes to collect the targeted victim’s sensitive data, and instruct an integrated AI model to analyze the harvested data, all within the compromised session.
items.detail:
Vulnérabilité critique affectant Windows.

Cisco Talos observed a new AI-integrated command-and-control (C2) framework in the wild called “NIK C2.” NIK C2 contains a Windows implant, using which, an actor can dump credentials, stream the victim's keystrokes to collect the targeted victim’s sensitive data, and instruct an integrated AI model to analyze the harvested data, all within the compromised session. In this framework, the actor has abused the OpenAI Chat Completions application programming interface (API), which is a HTTP endpoint that enables ChatGPT-style conversations programmatically. In addition to the features that enable theft, an actor can also deploy desktop screen-locking ransomware via the NIK C2 implant onto the victim machine, leading to a ransom demand in Bitcoin or USDT cryptocurrencies. NIK C2 reshapes adversary tradecraft by collapsing collection and exploitation into a single continuous session, effectively erasing the offline processing delays that historically granted defenders critical detection windows.  Such AI-enabled adversarial frameworks require defenders to move beyond traditional detection and embrace continuous behavioral vigilance as the new baseline. items.detail:
Incident de sécurité rapporté par The Record.

"No data was extracted,” a spokesperson for BAE Systems, a federal contractor, told Recorded Future News about its probe into a cyberattack against its systems for federal bankruptcy courts.

The Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts and an IT contractor said systems underpinning the federal bankruptcy courts are back online after a cyberattack two weeks ago caused outages.

The system, called the Bankruptcy Noticing Center (BNC), produces and transmits bankruptcy notices for all federal bankruptcy courts. The platform is maintained by British multinational BAE Systems, which said it has worked closely with the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts to restore the BNC.

“No other systems were affected. No data was extracted. There was no breach of any PII,” a spokesperson for BAE Systems told Recorded Future News.

No hackers ever took credit for the cyberattack, which was announced on October 22 and declared a “Bankruptcy Rules emergency” by federal court officials.

The emergency declaration allowed bankruptcy judges to extend deadlines and issue related orders that allowed them to operate around the BNC outage. The emergency declaration lasts 90 days through January 2027 unless it is ended by court officials.

“Although BNC has announced that services are beginning to resume, we anticipate that the emergency declaration will remain necessary throughout the restoration period,” the court said . “The declaration provides important flexibility to ensure that courts can address the effects of the outage and helps protect parties from potential prejudice resulting from delayed notice and related service disruptions.”

Incident de sécurité rapporté par The Record.

The Federal Public Service Finance (FPS Finance), which oversees taxation and other financial administration, said Wednesday that it was investigating the extent of the attack and had temporarily suspended access to MyMinfin, the country's main online platform for managing tax and financial affairs.

Belgium's finance ministry has taken its main online tax portal offline following a cyberattack, just days before a filing deadline for some taxpayers.

The Federal Public Service Finance (FPS Finance), which oversees taxation and other financial administration, said Wednesday that it was investigating the extent of the attack and had temporarily suspended access to MyMinfin, the country's main online platform for managing tax and financial affairs.

The shutdown comes ahead of an October 31 deadline for taxpayers reporting certain types of income. The agency said affected taxpayers would be given additional time to file their returns, with a revised deadline to be announced later.

Belgian authorities have not identified who was behind the attack or disclosed how the hackers may have gained access to government systems.

"Currently, there is no indication that a data breach has occurred or that any data has been stolen," FPS Finance said, adding that investigators were continuing to examine the possibility of data exposure.

The agency said it had taken the affected services offline as a precaution while specialists assessed the impact of the attack and carried out technical work to secure its systems. Several other government applications remained fully or partially operational.

Signal de veille — The Record.

General Motors agreed to pay $220 million to settle a lawsuit filed by a coalition of 36 state attorneys general who alleged the company unlawfully sold information about driver behavior to outside parties.

The data brokers then sold the sensitive data to insurers, affecting the prices drivers were charged for insurance, according to a press release from Washington Attorney General Nick Brown, who co-led the coalition’s efforts.

Beginning in 2016 and running through 2024, when the New York Times exposed the practice, GM allegedly enrolled millions of people in their “Smart Driver” program, allowing the auto giant to monitor their driving habits.

However, GM allegedly broke that promise by selling the information to data brokers despite contract language it signed indicating the brokers planned to profit by providing the data to insurers. GM did not tell participating customers they would do so, the suit alleged.

A GM spokesperson said in an emailed statement that the “agreement addresses Smart Driver, a product we ended in 2024, and reinforces steps we’ve taken to strengthen our privacy practices.”

“Safer, more helpful and personalized experiences are enabled by connected vehicle data, and GM is committed to being clear about what information is used, how it’s protected, and the choices customers have about what they share,” they said.

Most customers agreed to participate in the Smart Driver program at dealerships as they were purchasing cars, and many have described pressure tactics that convinced them to sign.

Signal de veille — The Record.

The Federal Trade Commission ordered nine food delivery, airline and ride-sharing companies to turn over detailed information on how they harness personal data to set individual consumer prices and employee compensation.

The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) on Wednesday ordered nine food delivery, airline, ride-sharing and retail companies to turn over detailed information on how they harness personal data to set individual consumer prices and employee compensation.

Orders were sent to JetBlue, Delta, United, Lyft, Uber, DoorDash, Instacart, Walmart and Target, the agency said. If the companies don’t respond, the agency can force them to comply in federal court.

The information will allow the agency to “assess whether the pricing for a ticket, ride share, food delivery or other product or service varies from one person to the next based on factors such as participation in loyalty programs or analysis of personal data by superintelligence algorithms,” the FTC said.

The companies employing gig workers also must give the agency the “inputs, tools and procedures” they deploy to tweak individual workers’ compensation and customer pricing based on personal data and unique characteristics, the agency said.

FTC officials plan to scrutinize the “opaque methodology” firms could be using to decide what to charge customers or pay individual gig workers, agency chair Andrew Ferguson said in a press release .

Consumers deserve to know if firms exploit their online browsing or other personal data to determine the highest price they think a given customer is willing to pay and the lowest price they think an individual worker will accept, he said.
